scope: Kenya soil classification (FAO/WRB reference groups with legacy FAO-1974 names and USDA equivalents)
Soil distribution by geographic area (county level)

data_quality.summary: Indicative, desk-based synthesis. Not field measurements and not a substitute for a soil test.
notes: The authoritative national reference is the Kenya Soil Survey Exploratory Soil Map (Sombroek, Braun and van der Pouw, 1982, 1:1,000,000). It is regional-scale and does not resolve individual farms.
Soil classes, texture, drainage, fertility and pH ranges are typical values compiled from the cited sources and general soil-science knowledge. pH ranges are expected ranges, not measurements.

County-to-soil links tagged 'supported' are tied to a retrieved source. Links tagged 'general_knowledge' follow the broad pattern of the exploratory map but were not individually confirmed; all counties carry verification_status needs_verification_against_kss_map.
Soils vary strongly with altitude and landform inside a county. Counties list the dominant and secondary groups only.
national_coverage_pct is only given for the ten most extensive groups, as read from a KARI slide deck (S4); verify before publishing.
follow_up_data_leads: KENSOTER / SOTER Kenya database (ISRIC) for polygon-level soil attributes
iSDAsoil and ISRIC SoilGrids for point-level pH, texture and organic carbon from latitude/longitude
KALRO county soil fertility surveys (the S4 deck reports sampling in Baringo, Bungoma, Busia and Bomet)
KALRO / Kenya Soil Survey detailed and reconnaissance reports (e.g. Mashuru, Kajiado)

ph.note: KSS treats soils below pH 5.5 as acid.

drainage.meaning: Water leaves very quickly (sandy or very shallow soils).
Water leaves readily but not too fast.
Wet for short periods in the rains.
Wet for significant periods; mottling common.
Wet for long periods; waterlogging is common.
Saturated at or near the surface most of the year.

reference_scales.fertility_note: Natural (inherent) fertility under typical conditions, not current nutrient status after years of cropping.

salinity_sodicity_risk.meaning: Salts or sodium not normally a problem.
Salt or gypsum build-up possible, especially under irrigation.
Saline or sodic; most crops fail without reclamation.

farmer_texture_crosswalk.note: Maps the four soil-type options in the FarmFriend form (index.html) to soil groups that commonly match. Derived from each soil's app_texture_class. Texture varies within a group, so this is a guide. Leptosols, Solonetz, Solonchaks and Gypsisols have no direct equivalent.

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Basic volcanic rocks (basalt, volcanic breccia, tuffs) and some basic metamorphic rock
formation.landscape: Highlands and upper volcanic slopes, undulating to steep

characteristics.colour: Dusky red to dark reddish brown
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Strong blocky ('nutty') structure; friable and porous despite high clay; sub-soil clay increases with depth
characteristics.organic_matter: Moderate to high in topsoil under forest or good management

fertility.notes: Among the best agricultural soils of the region; responds well to manure and fertilizer.

ph.notes: Most Nitisols are acidic (below pH 5.5) because soluble bases have leached.

management_pointers: Terrace and use cover to stop erosion
Test pH and lime where very acid

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Recent volcanic ash and other volcanic deposits
formation.landscape: Volcanic highlands (Mt Kenya, Aberdares, Mt Elgon, Mau), often steep and high-rainfall

characteristics.structure_and_physical: Very porous, very low bulk density, high water storage, crumb structure

drainage.notes: Free internal drainage because of high porosity.

fertility.notes: Naturally fertile where organic matter is high, but P is tied up and acidity grows with leaching.

ph.notes: Acidic from leaching of bases and aluminium; pH rises with ash freshness and in drier belts.

typical_use: Wheat and barley at higher altitude
key_constraints: Erosion and landslide risk on slopes
management_pointers: Place P fertilizer near the root zone
Liming and organic matter where acid

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Strongly weathered old rocks and sediments
formation.landscape: Gently undulating to undulating plateaus and uplands

characteristics.colour: Red, reddish brown or yellowish red
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Stable micro-aggregates; good physical condition and moisture-holding; rich in iron and aluminium oxides
characteristics.erosion_risk: Low to moderate when covered; surface crusting when bare

main_limiting_factors: Aluminium toxicity in very acid cases
fertility.notes: Physically excellent but chemically poor; needs regular nutrient replacement.

ph.notes: Typically acid; classed among Kenya's acid soils.

typical_use: Cashew and mango at the coast

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Old weathered rocks and sediments under humid climates

characteristics.texture: Sandy loam or clay loam topsoil over clay sub-soil
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Clay moves into sub-soil; surface seals and crusts; sub-soil less porous, which limits root spread

drainage.notes: Topsoil drains well; dense sub-soil can slow percolation.

fertility.notes: Strongly leached; productive only with liming and organic or mineral inputs.

ph.notes: Acid; Acrisols are named among Kenya's acid soil groups.

management_pointers: Lime to reach pH 5.5 or above

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Old weathered rocks and sediments in seasonally dry climates
formation.landscape: Gently sloping plains and pediments in semi-humid to semi-arid areas

characteristics.texture: Sandy loam to sandy clay loam over clay
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Clay accumulates in sub-soil; weak topsoil structure; prone to surface sealing and crusting

drainage.notes: Topsoil well drained; runoff is high when crusted.

fertility.notes: Moderate nutrient reserves but fragile surface; benefits from organic matter and water harvesting.

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Weathered rocks and alluvium in semi-arid zones
formation.landscape: Plains, plateaus and piedmont in semi-arid to sub-humid areas

characteristics.texture: Sandy loam to clay loam with clay-enriched sub-soil
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Clay-enriched B horizon; surface can seal; moderate structure

drainage.notes: Generally well drained; sub-soil slows deep percolation.

fertility.notes: Reasonable nutrient base; rainfall is usually the main limitation.

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Varied: volcanic, metamorphic and sedimentary materials
formation.landscape: Wide range, from hills and escarpments to plains

characteristics.structure_and_physical: Weakly developed horizons; moderate structure; often stony in hilly areas

fertility.notes: Fertility depends on parent rock and rainfall; often decent but variable.

ph.notes: Wide range; humic Cambisols can be acid, eutric and calcic types are near neutral to alkaline.

management_pointers: Test soil for pH and nutrients

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Basic volcanic rock, lake and river sediments rich in smectite clay
formation.landscape: Flat to very gently sloping plains, lake basins and valley floors

characteristics.structure_and_physical: Shrink-swell clays: wide deep cracks when dry; very sticky when wet and very hard when dry; narrow moisture window for tillage
characteristics.water_holding_capacity: High but much is held tightly by clay
characteristics.erosion_risk: Low to moderate (flooding and gullying in places)

drainage.notes: Very slow permeability; seasonal waterlogging and flooding common.

fertility.notes: Chemically rich in bases but difficult physically; needs good timing and drainage.

ph.notes: Neutral to alkaline; pellic types are often pH 7 or higher.

management_pointers: Ridge and furrow or raised beds
N and P fertilizer; improve drainage

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Old sediments and weathered rock on flat landscapes
formation.landscape: Flat to very gently undulating plains and plateaus

characteristics.texture: Coarse (sandy loam to loam) topsoil abruptly over dense clay
characteristics.colour: Light grey to brown topsoil; mottled sub-soil
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Abrupt texture change creates a perched water table; sub-soil dense and slowly permeable

drainage.notes: Seasonal waterlogging above dense clay, then rapid drying.

fertility.notes: Variable; works best with drainage, organic matter and careful crop choice.

ph.notes: Acid to slightly acid in topsoil.

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Volcanic and metamorphic rocks under grassland or savanna

characteristics.colour: Very dark brown to black topsoil
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Thick humus-rich topsoil with good crumb structure

drainage.notes: Good drainage with moderate water storage.

fertility.notes: Among Kenya's most productive grain soils when rainfall is reliable.

key_constraints: Declining organic matter under continuous cropping

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Recent river, lake and delta sediments
formation.landscape: Floodplains, deltas, river terraces and lake margins

characteristics.texture: Stratified silt, loam or clay layers
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Layered by flood events; weak structure; texture varies with depth

drainage.notes: Drainage varies by position; flooding is the main risk.

fertility.notes: Often productive under irrigation; fertility renewed by silt deposits.

ph.notes: Near neutral to alkaline; can be saline in dry areas.

management_pointers: Use organic matter to improve structure

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Wind-blown or coastal sands and coarse-grained sandstones and granites
formation.landscape: Coastal plains, dune belts and arid sand plains

drainage.notes: Water drains rapidly; leaching is high.

fertility.notes: Needs frequent small applications of water and nutrients and strong organic matter inputs.

ph.notes: Acid in humid coastal areas to alkaline where calcareous sand is present.

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Unconsolidated materials, often recent ash or colluvium
formation.landscape: Eroded or young landscapes, mostly arid and semi-arid

characteristics.texture: Sandy loam to loam, often stony
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Very little profile development; low organic matter

fertility.notes: Weakly developed soils, largely rangeland; crop use is risky without water.

ph.notes: Highly variable depending on parent material.

typical_use: Sorghum and millet in better-watered pockets

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Hard rock at or close to the surface

characteristics.structure_and_physical: Depth under 25 cm; abundant stones; poor root room

drainage.notes: Shallow, so water drains or runs off quickly.

fertility.notes: Not suited to regular cultivation; best for grazing, forestry and conservation.

ph.notes: Wide range depending on rock type.

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Calcareous parent material and carbonate-rich sediments in dry climates

characteristics.structure_and_physical: Secondary carbonate accumulation (sometimes hardened); low organic matter

drainage.notes: Well drained, but low rainfall means little water for crops.

main_limiting_factors: P, Zn and Fe less available at high pH
fertility.notes: Reasonable bases; water and micronutrient availability limit yields.

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Sediments rich in sodium in dry climates
formation.landscape: Plains, lake margins and depressions in arid and semi-arid areas

characteristics.texture: Loam topsoil over dense sodic clay
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Columnar or prismatic dense sub-soil; topsoil disperses and crusts; very low permeability

drainage.notes: Water ponds on the dense sodic layer.

fertility.notes: Largely unsuitable for crops without costly reclamation.

management_pointers: Gypsum plus drainage where reclamation is justified

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Salt-rich sediments in dry climates and around alkaline lakes
formation.landscape: Lake shores, salt flats and depressions in arid areas

characteristics.colour: Light grey to pale brown with salt crusts

drainage.notes: Poor drainage and shallow saline water tables are typical.

fertility.notes: Unsuitable for most crops; reclamation is difficult.

ph.notes: Alkaline and highly saline (check electrical conductivity as well as pH).

formation.parent_material: Gypsum-bearing sediments in very dry climates
formation.landscape: Arid plains in the north-east and north

characteristics.structure_and_physical: Gypsum accumulation can form crusts; weak structure

fertility.notes: Marginal for crops; irrigation can cause gypsum dissolution and subsidence.

classification.note: Sub-units (e.g. humic, rhodic, pellic, eutric) are not yet populated; add them as a later layer.

formation.parent_material: Alluvium and lake deposits in permanently or seasonally wet places
formation.landscape: Valley bottoms, swamps, lake shores and river deltas

characteristics.colour: Grey, blue-grey or olive with rust mottles
characteristics.structure_and_physical: Saturated for long periods; reduced iron colours
characteristics.organic_matter: Moderate to high (accumulating in wet places)

drainage.notes: Water table at or near the surface for much of the year.

fertility.notes: Potentially fertile but needs drainage; many wetlands should be protected.

ph.notes: Acid to neutral depending on setting.
